name: Single-Arm Cable Face Pull
description: The single-arm cable face pull uses one hand on the rope or handle to perform the face pull movement unilaterally. The single-arm version allows independent training of each rear delt and external rotator, is more effective at correcting left-right imbalances than bilateral face pulls, and allows slightly greater range of motion as the torso can rotate slightly without losing the training stimulus.

execution.starting_position: Set a cable pulley to upper face level. Attach a single handle. Grasp with one hand, arm extended toward the pulley. Stand facing the cable.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the pulley at approximately eye level. Light load only — rear delts and external rotators are small muscles.
steps: Step 1: Begin with arm extended toward the cable.
Step 2: Pull the handle toward the same-side ear/face, driving the elbow wide.
Step 3: At peak, externally rotate the shoulder — thumb points behind and down.
Step 5: Return under control. Complete all reps on one side before switching.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the pull. Inhale returning.
common_mistakes: Pulling to the chest instead of the face — keep the hand at face level
Omitting external rotation — the ER at peak is essential for shoulder health benefit
safety_considerations: Light loads only — high reps with light weight are more appropriate than heavy low reps
Suitable as a warm-up or shoulder health accessory
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension to hand at face level with full external rotation.
coaching_cues: Pull to the ear, not the chin
Thumb points behind you at the top
